items.question: i think the overall app is there, however i cannot export and customize with custom fonts, colors. I want the features of the full app Tableau Desktop. can you do that?
items.answer:
I'll add the two things you named now: a proper Export menu and formatting (fonts, colours, number styles). Then I'll be straight about the rest of the full app. First I'm checking what tools I have to work with.Yes, I can add exporting and custom fonts and colours. Matching every feature of the full Tableau Desktop is different: it has grown over about 20 years, so it can't all be rebuilt in one go. What I can do is add its features in rounds, most-used first.

**What your version can already export.** The File menu has two export options:
- **Export sheet data as CSV**, which saves the numbers behind the current chart as a spreadsheet file.
- **Save picture of window (PNG)**, which saves a picture of the whole window, not just the chart.

Those options are only in the menu and limited, so I'd improve them.

**Next round: exporting and formatting**
- An **Export** button in the toolbar that can save:
  - only the chart or dashboard as a picture (PNG) or as a PDF
  - the chart's data as CSV
  - all of the underlying data
- A **Format** panel for each sheet:
  - **Fonts:** choose any font installed on your computer (or load a font file), set the size of titles, labels and axes, and choose text colour.
  - **Colours:** pick a colour scheme (including a colourblind-safe one), set any single value's colour by hand, choose the colour scale for numbers, and set the chart background.
  - **Numbers:** show values as plain numbers, currency or percent, with a set number of decimal places.
  - **Layout:** show or hide grid lines, and edit chart titles.
  - An **Apply to all sheets** button so a whole workbook can share one look.

**Main Tableau features still missing, in the order I'd suggest:**
1. Opening Excel files, and joining or combining two data files.
2. Interactive dashboards, where clicking one chart filters the others, plus filter controls on the dashboard.
3. Advanced calculations:
   - running totals and percent of total
   - values that can be adjusted with a slider or dropdown
   - IF/THEN formulas
   - grouping values together, and sets
4. Maps (from place names or latitude and longitude).
5. Analytics: trend lines, reference lines and forecasts.
6. Two measures on one chart, more chart types (such as histograms and box plots), and story-style slideshows.
7. Live connections to databases. Publishing to the web is the hardest piece; a free version would need its own sharing service.

Just say "go" and I'll start with the exporting and formatting round, or tell me if you'd rather I start with Excel files or interactive dashboards.

items.question: i cannot edit or customize the chart, mark size, colors, etc.
items.answer:
I'll look at how the Marks card is wired to find out why your changes aren't showing up.You're right, and it's a gap in what I built, not something you're doing wrong. Right now there are only a few ways to change how a chart looks:

- **Colours can't be picked at all.** Every chart uses one fixed set of colours. You can choose *what* decides the colours by dragging a field onto the Color box, but you can't change the colours themselves. Clicking the Color box does nothing.
- **The "Mark size" slider only works on some charts.** It changes bars, dots and scatter plots. It does nothing on lines, areas, pies, tables or heat maps. Two of the four example sheets are a line chart and a heat map, so moving it there looks broken.
- **Clicking Size or Detail does nothing either.** Clicking Label only turns the number labels on and off. In the original, clicking these boxes opens settings, so it's natural to expect that.
- **Chart titles, gridlines and the legend can't be changed.** The only exception: the title follows the sheet's name, so double-clicking a sheet's tab at the bottom renames it.
- **Some options are hidden behind a right-click.** Right-clicking a coloured field on Columns or Rows lets you switch Sum to Average or Year to Month. Nothing on screen tells you this.

I can't change the app in this chat, because I can only look at the files here. When you want it fixed, say "go" and I'll:

1. Open a settings box when you click Color, Size or Label. Color would let you pick a colour scheme, change any single colour, and set see-through and outlines. Size would get a slider that works on every chart type, including line thickness. Label would let you set label size.
2. Add a Format button for the chart title, gridlines and legend.
3. Show a hint that you can right-click fields for more options.

items.question: no, still not able to customize the colors nor the typography. not even available. also there are no tooltips when mousover the chart.
items.answer:
I'll look at how the charts handle the mouse, and what the toolkit offers for fonts and colour pickers.You're right on both counts. I checked the app, and I couldn't fix it in this reply because this session can only read the files.

**Tooltips:** I did write a hover box that shows the exact values under the mouse, and a highlight on the bar or point you're over. A mistake keeps both from ever appearing: an invisible layer sits on top of every chart, and it catches the mouse before the chart can see it. The dashboard has the same problem. The fix is small: remove that layer and make the box appear straight away instead of waiting for the mouse to stop.

**Colours and fonts:** These were never built. The colours and text sizes are fixed inside the app, and there's no screen to change them. That was a gap I didn't mention in my summary, and I should have.

Here's what I'd add, as a **Format** panel that opens next to Show Me:
- **Colours:** pick a colour set (default, colour-blind friendly, warm, cool, pastel, greys). You could also change the colour of any single item, such as making "Tech" red, set the colour used when nothing is on Color, and choose the shading for heat maps.
- **Typography:** choose a font, including any font installed on your computer. You could set the text size for labels and axes, and the title's size and colour.
- **Chart look:** background colour and gridlines on or off. An "apply to all sheets" button would copy the formatting to every sheet, and it would all be saved with your workbook.

Say "go" and I'll build the tooltip fix and the Format panel, then check both with pictures of the app running.

items.question: fix the customizing chart function. i have to be able to edit the typography and colors of the chart
items.answer:
Let me look at how chart customization is currently built so I can answer accurately.Short answer: right now the app has **no chart customization for typography or colors** — nothing is broken, it was never built. I checked the actual code to be sure:

**Observed (in the code):**
- The worksheet stores only data choices: which fields go on which shelves, mark type, sorting, whether labels show, and mark size. No font or color settings exist in a sheet (`/home/luis/Documents/Craft Anything/tableaudesktop-2026-3-0/app/src/model.rs`).
- All chart colors are fixed constants — the 8-color category palette, the blue sequential ramp, and the red/blue diverging ramp in `/home/luis/Documents/Craft Anything/tableaudesktop-2026-3-0/app/src/chart.rs` (top of the file: `CAT`, `SEQ`, `DIV_NEG`, `DIV_POS`, plus ink/grid colors).
- All text in charts uses one default font size; there's no font family, size, or style option anywhere in the painting code (`app/src/paint.rs`).
- The only customization dialogs that exist are rename, filter, calculated field, file chooser, and About (`app/src/app/dialogs.rs`). There is no "format chart" or "edit colors" window.

**What I'd change** (you can ask for this as a change and I'll build it):

1. **Format panel / dialog** — a "Format Chart" window per sheet with:
   - *Typography:* font size sliders for title, axis labels, and marks/labels (egui ships with limited font families, so it would be size/weight rather than arbitrary fonts, unless we bundle extra font files).
   - *Colors:* a color picker for the main mark color, a choice of built-in palettes (the current Tableau-like one plus a few alternatives), pickers for the sequential/diverging ramp end colors when a measure is on Color, and colors for background, grid lines, and axis text.
2. **Store it on the sheet** — add a small `style` block to the sheet model so choices are remembered and saved into workbook files.
3. **Use it when painting** — have `chart.rs`/`paint.rs` read the sheet's style instead of the hardcoded constants, falling back to the current look when nothing is customized.

Say the word and I'll implement it as a change.
